::: proof
Write $\mu_i \eqdef t_i \expf{\eta(\vx_i)}$ for observation $i$'s mean.
Each $y_i$ has a Poisson distribution with mean $\mu_i$,
so the [log-likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-loglik) is

$$
\ba
\llik(\vb)
&= \sumin \logf{\frac{\mu_i^{y_i} \expf{-\mu_i}}{y_i!}}
&& \text{(independence; Poisson PMF)} \\
&= \sumin \paren{y_i \logf{\mu_i} - \mu_i - \logf{y_i!}}
&& \text{(log of a product and quotient)} \\
&= \sumin \paren{y_i \paren{\logf{t_i} + \sum_{k=0}^p x_{ik} \b_k} - \mu_i - \logf{y_i!}}
&& \text{(substitute } \logf{\mu_i} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Each mean has derivative
$\deriv{\b_j} \mu_i = \mu_i x_{ij}$
(chain rule for the exponential),
so the partial derivative of $\llik$ with respect to $\b_j$ is:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\b_j} \llik(\vb)
&= \sumin \paren{y_i x_{ij} - \mu_i x_{ij}}
&& \text{(differentiate term by term)} \\
&= \sumin x_{ij} \, y_i - \sumin x_{ij} \, \mu_i
&& \text{(distribute the sum over the terms)}
\ea
$$

The maximum likelihood estimate $\evb$ maximizes $\llik$ over all of $\reals^{p+1}$,
so it solves the [score equations](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-score-equation)
$\deriv{\b_j} \llik(\evb) = 0$ for every $j$.
At $\vb = \evb$, each $\mu_i$ equals $\emu_i$, so:

$$
\ba
0
&= \sumin x_{ij} \, y_i - \sumin x_{ij} \, \emu_i
&& \text{(score equation at } \evb \text{)} \\
\sumin x_{ij} \, \emu_i
&= \sumin x_{ij} \, y_i
&& \text{(add } \textstyle\sumin x_{ij} \, \emu_i \text{ to both sides)}
\ea
$$

For $j = 0$, every $x_{i0} = 1$,
which gives $\sumin y_i = \sumin \emu_i$.
If $x_j$ is a group indicator,
the terms with $x_{ij} = 0$ vanish from both sides,
and the terms with $x_{ij} = 1$ are exactly the group's observations.
:::
